bull.b: Commercial fleet adoption moving from pilots to direct deployment supports a more repeatable sales pipeline and broadens the company beyond weaker RV demand. Validated fuel and maintenance savings may strengthen customer economics, helping trucking become a durable growth channel.

Dakota Lithium expands Dragonfly’s addressable market and complements Battle Born across applications and price points. Rebuilding inventory and distribution could create cross-selling and broader channel reach, while planned use of existing infrastructure may support operating leverage.

Lower operating expenses show tangible progress in cost discipline and reduce the expense base required to support revenue. If maintained alongside trucking growth and Dakota integration, these savings can improve the path toward management’s goal of sustainable positive adjusted EBITDA.

bear.b: Large operating losses and sustained negative cash generation weaken the company’s ability to fund operations internally. Continued cash burn can force reliance on debt or equity capital, limiting strategic flexibility and making progress toward durable profitability more difficult.

Negative equity signals substantial capitalization strain, while the Nasdaq remediation deadline adds an important structural financing and listing risk. Failure to restore required equity could trigger delisting proceedings, potentially reducing market access and stakeholder liquidity.

The company remains materially exposed to a declining RV market, which has already reduced sales, gross profit, and gross margin. Continued weak OEM and direct-to-consumer demand can offset growth in trucking and delay the revenue scale needed to absorb fixed operating costs.
